title: View Helper Pattern
oneLiner: Moves formatting and display logic out of a view/template into a dedicated helper, so the view stays focused purely on layout.

hero.name: The Stagehand
hero.catchphrase: The view just displays. I do the formatting work backstage.
hero.power: Handles all the formatting and display-logic legwork behind the scenes, so templates only ever describe layout, never computation.
hero.weakness: Scatter formatting logic across too many uncoordinated helpers and it fragments the same way tangled inline template logic did.
hero.origin: The Stagehand appeared after a product page template was riddled with inline date-formatting, currency-formatting, and truncation logic, making the markup unreadable and impossible to test.

story.problem: A product page template is full of inline logic: date formatting, currency formatting, text truncation — all mixed directly into the markup, making it unreadable and impossible to unit test.
story.solution: The Stagehand moves that logic into a `ProductViewHelper` class with methods like `formatPrice()` and `truncateDescription()`. The template just calls these methods — no computation happens in the markup itself.
story.result: The template becomes purely declarative layout. All the formatting logic lives in one testable class, reusable across every template that needs it.

before: Formatting logic is inlined directly into template markup
The same formatting logic is duplicated across templates
Formatting rules can't be unit tested independently
after: Templates only describe layout, calling helper methods
Formatting logic lives in one reusable, shared class
Formatting rules are independently unit testable

panels.label: The Problem
panels.caption: A product page template has fifteen lines of inline date and currency formatting mixed directly into the markup.
panels.speaker: Developer
panels.dialogue: This template is unreadable. I can't tell where the layout ends and the currency-formatting logic begins.

panels.label: The Hero Arrives
panels.caption: The Stagehand appears backstage, quietly preparing everything the view will need.
panels.speaker: The Stagehand
panels.dialogue: The view shouldn't compute anything. Let me handle the formatting backstage — your template just displays the result.

panels.label: Pattern Power
panels.caption: ProductViewHelper.formatPrice(product) and .truncateDescription(product) do all the computation. The template just calls them.
panels.speaker: The Stagehand
panels.dialogue: Call helper.formatPrice(product) in your markup. All the currency logic lives in one tested class — the template never sees it.

panels.label: The Result
panels.caption: The template shrinks to pure layout markup, with formatting logic now unit tested separately.
panels.speaker: Developer
panels.dialogue: The template is readable again, and the formatting logic finally has real unit tests.

useWhen: Templates or views are accumulating inline formatting/computation logic that makes them hard to read.
The same formatting rules (currency, dates, truncation) are duplicated across multiple templates.
You want formatting logic to be independently unit testable, separate from rendering.
avoidWhen: The view only ever displays raw, pre-formatted data with no computation needed.
Your templating framework already provides clean, built-in formatting primitives that make a separate helper redundant.
The formatting is truly one-off and used in exactly one place — a dedicated helper class is unnecessary ceremony.
commonMistakes: Letting view helpers grow into a dumping ground for unrelated business logic instead of staying focused on presentation formatting.
Creating one helper per template instead of sharing helpers for genuinely common formatting logic (currency, dates) across the app.
Not testing helper methods independently, missing the exact benefit that separating them from the template was supposed to provide.
Confusing View Helper with Facade — View Helper specifically targets presentation formatting; Facade simplifies access to a broader subsystem.
explanation.realWorldExample: Rails view helpers, template engine 'filters' (Jinja2, Handlebars helpers), and React custom hooks like `useFormattedDate()` that keep formatting logic out of JSX are all View Helper in practice.

conversation.speaker: Mentor
conversation.message: Isn't this just... a utility function?

conversation.speaker: The Stagehand
conversation.message: At small scale, sure. I matter once a template accumulates ENOUGH formatting logic that it starts obscuring the actual layout — that's my cue to pull it all out into one coherent, testable place.

conversation.speaker: Mentor
conversation.message: When do I stop adding helpers?

conversation.speaker: The Stagehand
conversation.message: When a helper starts doing business logic instead of formatting — validating orders, calculating discounts. That's not presentation anymore. Keep me strictly backstage, handling only how things LOOK.

codeBattle.scenario: Your dashboard has twelve different templates, each independently reimplementing the same date-formatting and number-formatting logic inline, and a recent locale bug had to be fixed in all twelve places separately.
codeBattle.question: Which hero should you call?
codeBattle.explanation: The Stagehand centralizes the date/number formatting logic in one shared helper class, so the locale bug fix happens once instead of twelve times.

quiz.question: What does View Helper move out of templates?
quiz.explanation: View Helper's whole purpose is separating 'how to compute the display value' from 'how to lay it out'.

quiz.question: What's a key benefit of moving formatting logic into a View Helper class?
options: The logic becomes independently unit testable, separate from rendering
It makes the template file larger
It removes the need for any templates at all
It automatically translates text into other languages
quiz.answer: The logic becomes independently unit testable, separate from rendering
quiz.explanation: Extracting formatting logic into its own class/methods makes it trivially testable without needing to render a view at all.

quiz.question: What's a common mistake when using View Helper?
options: Letting the helper accumulate business logic instead of staying focused on presentation formatting
Sharing a helper's formatting methods across multiple templates
Unit testing the helper's methods independently
Extracting date formatting out of a template
quiz.answer: Letting the helper accumulate business logic instead of staying focused on presentation formatting
quiz.explanation: A helper should stay about 'how things look', not become a dumping ground for logic that belongs elsewhere.

quiz.question: What's a real-world example of View Helper?
options: Rails view helpers or template engine formatting filters
quiz.answer: Rails view helpers or template engine formatting filters
quiz.explanation: These are widely-used, real-world implementations of exactly this idea: keeping formatting logic out of raw templates.
